title: Global section-algebra Proj embedding from etale local canonical maps
statement:
Let $S,T$ be schemes [def-pc-scheme], let $X$ be an algebraic space over $S$ [def-trf-algebraic-space], let $f:X\to T$ be a quasi-compact separated morphism over $S$ in the terminology of [lem-trf-space-qc-separated-etale-local], and let $L$ be a line module on $X$. Let $\{g_i:T_i\to T\}_{i\in I}$ be a jointly surjective etale family of schemes such that $X_i=X\times_TT_i$ is a scheme for every $i$. Put $f_i:X_i\to T_i$ and let $L_i$ be the ordinary invertible module [def-sc-invertible-module] corresponding to $L|_{X_i}$ [def-trf-space-module-scheme-restriction]. For each $i$, form the ordinary canonical graded section algebra $\mathcal A_i=\bigoplus_{d\geq0}(f_i)_*L_i^{\otimes d}$ and its evaluation homomorphism $\psi_i:f_i^*\mathcal A_i\to\bigoplus_{d\geq0}L_i^{\otimes d}$. Suppose $U(\psi_i)=X_i$ and the canonical map $r_i:X_i\to\operatorname{Proj}_{T_i}(\mathcal A_i)$ is an open immersion, with the generation locus and canonical map defined by [lem-trf-space-line-module-proj-map].
Here $f_*$ and $f^*$ mean direct image and tensor pullback on small etale ringed topoi; passage to Zariski modules uses the scheme-site equivalence in [lem-trf-space-section-algebra-etale-base-change]. Then $\mathcal A=\bigoplus_{d\geq0}f_*L^{\otimes d}$ is a quasi-coherent graded Zariski $\mathcal O_T$-algebra [def-weil-pbc-quasi-coherent-algebra] [def-weil-pbc-graded-sheaf-structures], with canonical graded isomorphisms $g_i^*\mathcal A\simeq\mathcal A_i$ identifying the restriction of its evaluation map $\psi$ with $\psi_i$. The comparison in degree $d$ sends a section of $f_*L^{\otimes d}$ to its restriction, and evaluation then gives the same local section of $L_i^{\otimes d}$. The relative Proj $P=\operatorname{Proj}_T(\mathcal A)$ [def-nagata-relative-proj] is a scheme. Its canonical map $r:U(\psi)\to P$ has $U(\psi)=X$ and is an open immersion. Under $\operatorname{Proj}_{T_i}(\mathcal A_i)\simeq P\times_TT_i$, the maps $r_i$ are its base changes. In particular $X$ is a scheme. For this resulting scheme, $\mathcal A$, $\psi$, and $r$ agree with the ordinary Zariski section algebra, its evaluation homomorphism, and its ordinary canonical map for the invertible module corresponding to $L$.

proof.text: Apply space_section_algebra_etale_base_change to get A, its ordinary-scheme agreement, and normalized base-change models. Present A by section_proj_model_presentation, retaining exactly the same section algebra.

For each supplied local model, apply section_proj_model_comparison to the normalized base-change model just obtained. This gives the local ordinary-scheme agreement, beta, D, its degree equation and IsBaseChange. Choose these comparisons for all i. PullbackData.isPullback gives the Cartesian relative-Proj square of each D.

Apply space_line_proj_etale_descent to these coefficient data, the cover and the supplied local canonical open immersions. It returns full generation and the global canonical representable open immersion with the local component equations.

Representability of etale morphisms is stable under the given source pullback squares. The cartesian realization restricted to each resulting etale test is its ordinary Zariski restriction, by etaleLinePresentation_schemeRestriction. The line presentation behind lineTestFamily is linePresentation, whose line is L by exists_linePresentation.

Test the global representable open immersion over the identity of its scheme target. In this pullback square the projection to X is an isomorphism. Its representing scheme U, the scheme open immersion q and this isomorphism e satisfy the Yoneda equation by commutativity. Isomorphisms are etale; apply the same restriction theorem to e.
